summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic and groin pain, burning at the catheter site, and malaise, concerning for recurrent urinary tract infection. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter due to hypotonic bladder and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Urinalysis showed infection, and he was started on empiric IV antibiotics. Urine culture grew Acinetobacter baumannii and Enterobacter cloacae, both sensitive to ciprofloxacin. He transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and completed a catheter change during treatment. His mental confusion on admission resolved quickly and was attributed to sundowning rather than infection. A chest X-ray showed a worsening left pleural effusion but no pneumonia, consistent with his chronic asbestosis. He was discharged to a rehab facility to complete a 14-day course of ciprofloxacin, with plans to follow up with urology and infectious disease for recurrent UTI prevention. His chronic conditions, including CAD, diabetes, hypertension, and a monitored renal mass, remained stable.
